report.summary: Bootstrap module: shadow run logic, source refresh, gate discrimination. 7 symbols, 3 checkable claims, 2 uncheckable claims.
risks: refresh_sources line 111 | high | runner param type hint says Callable but docstring says tests can use it; actual subprocess fallback may mask errors if runner returns unexpected type | Check that all callers of refresh_sources provide a runner that returns a tuple[int, str]
refresh_sources line 130 | medium | _run function captures only last 600 chars of stdout+stderr; long error messages may be truncated | Verify that 600 chars is sufficient for diagnostic detail

handoff.purpose: Define bootstrap module docstring, constants, SourceRefresh, GateDiscrimination, refresh_sources, and _gate_binding.

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Resolved path to project root (two directories up from this file).

symbols.name: DISCRIMINATION_REL_PATH
symbols.note: Relative path where discrimination measurement is recorded; absence means unproven.

symbols.name: CRITICAL_DEFECT_CLASSES
symbols.note: Tuple of defect classes that must be killed completely for gate to be proven.

symbols.name: KILL_RATE_FLOOR
symbols.note: Minimum overall kill rate (0.80) for a proven gate.

symbols.name: SourceRefresh
symbols.note: Dataclass recording attempted source regeneration and its outcome.

symbols.name: _recorded_head
symbols.note: Reads JSON from path and returns repo_state.head if present.

symbols.name: refresh_sources
symbols.note: Regenerates derived sources (map) so the circle can start. Returns tuple of SourceRefresh.

symbols.name: GateDiscrimination
symbols.note: Dataclass recording whether a gate has been shown to discriminate.

symbols.name: _gate_binding
symbols.note: Validates and canonicalises a discrimination gate description.

claims.text: A shadow run produces candidates and says exactly how much they are worth, which today is: 'the configured gate command ran'. It refuses to render a green gate as evidence of quality, and it refuses to promote.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements candidate production, gate running, or promotion refusal.

claims.text: Both gates were correct. The structural problem they expose is worse than either: the loop INVALIDATES ITS OWN INPUTS EVERY TIME IT SUCCEEDS.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows the loop or its invalidation; only source refresh is present.

claims.text: Regeneration is step zero of the circle, not a chore beside it.
claims.why: The function refresh_sources is defined and called as step zero before any attempt.

claims.text: It knows whether the gate can discriminate, and refuses to guess. ... Until such a measurement exists for the current revision, the answer is unproven, and unproven blocks promotion.
claims.why: GateDiscrimination dataclass is defined, but no code in this chunk uses it to block promotion.

claims.text: It never writes the primary checkout. Inherited from attempt module, which has no apply path at all, and asserted here again because this module is the one that would be tempted.
claims.why: No code in this chunk writes to primary checkout; but the claim refers to the attempt module which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A regeneration command that exits 0 without making the source fresh is the failure mode that would otherwise be reported as success
claims.why: refresh_sources checks after is not None even if exit code is 0; see line 149-151.

claims.text: runner exists so tests can drive this without invoking the real generator; the product path uses a subprocess, because the generator is a CLI verb and re-implementing it here would create a second, drifting copy
claims.why: refresh_sources accepts runner param; if runner is None it falls back to subprocess.run.

claims.text: A repository that explicitly disabled that source chose the curated queue as its authority; regenerating map anyway would violate both that declaration and shadow mode's no-surprise boundary before an attempt even starts.
claims.why: Lines 113-118 check map_mode and return early if disabled.

claims.text: Exit 0 is NOT the success criterion. The criterion is that the artefact now stamps a revision, because that is what the consumer checks.
claims.why: Line 149: succeeded = (code == 0 and after is not None).

claims.text: A discrimination score belongs to the exact command that produced it. A receipt which merely says 'pytest' -- or whose gate_scope disagrees with its paths -- is not evidence about any gate.
claims.why: The function validates argv, paths, scope, and checks receipt argv matches production pytest argv.

claims.text: Receipt bindings are narrower than requested bindings: this corpus tool measures only the real pytest gate, while a candidate may request a custom command such as the docref verifier. The latter is valid as a request but cannot match a pytest receipt.
claims.why: Lines 204-210: if receipt, allowed_scopes excludes 'custom-command'; also checks argv equals expected pytest argv.

observations.what: refresh_sources imports daedalus.config.resolve_project and daedalus.spine.picker._picker_source_mode, but those modules are not shown in this chunk; their behavior is assumed.

The _run function inside refresh_sources catches Exception and returns code 1 with a string detail; this may mask unexpected errors like KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit which are not Exception subclasses.
The docstring for _gate_binding says 'A receipt which merely says pytest' but the function checks argv against pytest_gate_argv; it does not check if the receipt literally contains the word 'pytest'.
